SMTO-EXE-0021 — SMTO saved your choice to continue from how things are now

GUID: 175e1521-8c98-4232-9f7a-46d0b7847ff6
Slug: resource-reconciliation-accepted-current-state
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • You chose to accept things as they are now after an earlier job blocked your task. SMTO recorded that choice so the task can go on. The earlier job's history is kept unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue; the command that was waiting can now start. Your choice released the hold the earlier job had on the same files or resources.
  2. If you're unsure what the earlier job left behind, check those files or settings before the task makes more changes. Accepting the current state doesn't undo or redo anything the earlier job did.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card goes away and the task runs its next command.

If it still fails

  • If the task stays blocked, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't make the same choice again; it is already saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway accepted and persisted a current-state baseline for the blocker set after verifying correlation, blocker revision, ended uncertain operations and the absence of conflicting live peers.

What this means

  • The Gateway accepted a current-state baseline after checking correlation, blocker revision, ended uncertain operations, released claims and absence of conflicting live peers, then persisted the decision. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway accepted a current-state baseline after checking correlation, blocker revision, ended uncertain operations, released claims and absence of conflicting live peers, then persisted the decision.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the persisted baseline event, its resource revision and the original operation's retained outcome.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is needed. The decision is stored as baseline_decision_id on the source job and as effect_reconciliation on each blocker; historical execution outcomes are unchanged. Inspect the Gateway job records if you need to audit it.

Retry and execution caution

  • This condition does not authorize a retry or require an automatic action.

How to verify the fix

  • The current-state decision is saved for the matching resources while historical execution facts remain intact.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
